front_blocks.md: Define **saturated** (as used for hydrocarbons).

back_blocks.md: A **saturated** hydrocarbon contains only **single carbon-carbon bonds** — there are no double bonds between carbon atoms.

cards.back_md: A **saturated** hydrocarbon contains only **single carbon-carbon bonds** — there are no double bonds between carbon atoms.

front_blocks.md: Alkanes belong to a group of **..........** hydrocarbons, meaning they have only **..........** carbon-carbon bonds.

back_blocks.md: Alkanes belong to a group of **saturated** hydrocarbons, meaning they have only **single** carbon-carbon bonds.

cards.front_md: Alkanes belong to a group of **..........** hydrocarbons, meaning they have only **..........** carbon-carbon bonds.
cards.back_md: Alkanes belong to a group of **saturated** hydrocarbons, meaning they have only **single** carbon-carbon bonds.

front_blocks.md: Why are alkanes described as **saturated**?

back_blocks.md: Alkanes are described as **saturated** because they contain only **single carbon-carbon bonds**. There are no double bonds between carbon atoms, so the molecule cannot take on any more hydrogen atoms.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Pentane has the molecular formula C<sub>5</sub>H<sub>12</sub>.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
Pentane is the fifth **alkane**. Using the general formula C<sub>n</sub>H<sub>2n+2</sub> with n = 5 gives C<sub>5</sub>H<sub>12</sub>.

front_blocks.md: What types of reactions can alkanes undergo?

back_blocks.md: Alkanes can undergo **combustion**, can be **cracked** into smaller molecules, and can react with **halogens** in the presence of light.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Alkanes are highly reactive compounds.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Alkanes are generally **unreactive** compounds, though they do undergo combustion, cracking, and reactions with halogens.

front_blocks.md: What is the main component of natural gas?

back_blocks.md: The main component of natural gas is **methane**, the simplest **alkane** with the molecular formula CH<sub>4</sub>.

cards.front_md: What is the main component of natural gas?
cards.back_md: The main component of natural gas is **methane**, the simplest **alkane** with the molecular formula CH<sub>4</sub>.

front_blocks.md: What is a **substitution reaction**?

back_blocks.md: A **substitution reaction** is one in which one atom is **swapped** (replaced) with another atom.

cards.back_md: A **substitution reaction** is one in which one atom is **swapped** (replaced) with another atom.

front_blocks.md: What conditions are needed for alkanes to react with halogens?

back_blocks.md: Alkanes react with halogens in the presence of **ultraviolet (UV) radiation**. Without UV light, this **substitution reaction** does not occur.

front_blocks.md: In the presence of UV radiation, methane reacts with bromine to form **..........** and **..........**.

back_blocks.md: In the presence of UV radiation, methane reacts with bromine to form **bromomethane** and **hydrogen bromide**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Alkanes react with halogens in the dark.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Alkanes only react with halogens in the presence of **ultraviolet (UV) radiation**. The reaction does not occur in the dark.

front_blocks.md: What type of compounds are formed when alkanes react with halogens?

back_blocks.md: The products are called **halogenoalkanes** (or haloalkanes). These are compounds in which one or more hydrogen atoms of the alkane have been replaced by a **halogen** atom.

cards.back_md: The products are called **halogenoalkanes** (or haloalkanes). These are compounds in which one or more hydrogen atoms of the alkane have been replaced by a **halogen** atom.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Chlorine can react with methane in the presence of UV light to form chloromethane.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
Methane reacts with **chlorine** under UV light in a **substitution reaction**, producing chloromethane and hydrogen chloride.

front_blocks.md: What are halogenoalkanes used for?

back_blocks.md: Halogenoalkanes are used as **solvents**, **refrigerants**, propellants, and **pharmaceuticals**.
